newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures begin mixed, eye T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures begin mixed, eye T-bonds.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures opened mixed, wary of Treasury bond weakness but looking ahead to the next batch of U.S. data.
Treasury bond futures sagged after July U.S. jobs data early and cast a slightly bearish shadow on stock indices.

July jobs rose 316,000, compared with a 193,000 forecast and an upwardly revised 228,000 in June. Average hourly earnings were flat at $12.23 and the jobless rate fell to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent.
Treasury bond futures fell after the data, but held yesterday's low of 116-04/32.
Standard and Poor's 500 futures began slightly higher, chopped around briefly, then posted a new session peak.
"I said yesterday that you weren't really going to knock us down unless you've got jobs above 400,000," an S&P 500 futures trader said.

He said the market would focus on National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) data at 0900 CDT/1400 GMT, zoning in on the prices-paid component after a strong Chicago purchasing managers prices-paid figure on Thursday.
Chicago's prices-paid index rose to 61.6 in July from 53.7 in June.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average overall July NAPM estimate of 56.1 from 55.7 in the previous report.
"Really, we're looking for any inflation indications," another S&P 500 futures trader said.
Also at 0900 CDT is final July University of Michigan consumer sentiment and two inflation gauges.
The all-time high in September S&Ps is at 963.90, with support seen at 956.00, 953.00 and 951.00, traders said.

At 0847 CDT, Sept S&P 500s were up 1.45 pts to 959.40, Nikkei fell 475.0 pts to 19,900.0, Midcap 400s rose 0.80 to 316.90, Russell rose 0.70 to 416.25, and NASDAQ rose 7.00 to 1121.50. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
